name: MailerLite
summary: Email marketing for small senders and creators: drag-and-drop campaigns from templates, automations, subscriber groups and a free plan for small lists.
best_for: small senders and creators who want a simple newsletter tool with a free plan and a template editor
skip_if: you need deep automation, or you want to know exactly what the account does after the trial before you sign up
honest_knock: The free plan stops at 250 subscribers, and prices rise with the subscriber count. During our trial the Comfort checkout asked for the full amount immediately with 14 trial days left, and Plan and Billing showed the Free plan while the header said trial, so check what you are buying before you enter a card. Without a connected domain, mail goes out from a temporary address. Three automation templates are marked Premium.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Comfort (500 subscribers) · Comfort $12/mo and Power $25/mo for 500 subscribers, monthly, on the MailerLite upgrade screen read 22 November 2026
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-22 in the MailerLite app, USD unless stated) Free: up to 250 subscribers and 2,500 emails, 0 a month. For 500 subscribers, billed monthly: Comfort $12 (5,000 emails a month, 50 automations, 10 forms, 3 user seats) and Power $25 (unlimited emails). Billed yearly in EUR: Comfort EUR 9.90 a month (EUR 118.80 a year) and Power EUR 17.10 a month (EUR 205.20 a year). Enterprise is custom. The Comfort monthly checkout, which charged in EUR, showed EUR 11 plus 21% VAT, EUR 13.31 due now, with the next charge on 22 December 2026. Prices rise with the subscriber count. Black Friday: 26% off annual plans with the code LITEFRIDAY26 (Comfort $144 a year to $107, Power $300 to $222), ends 18 December 2026.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 22 November 2026 in the MailerLite web app on a new 14-day trial account, with the interface in English. We added a subscriber to a new group, built a campaign from a template and sent ourselves a test email, opened the automation templates, read the plans and opened the Comfort checkout. We did not send a campaign and did not pay.
findings: Dashboard: the 14-day trial opened with a Lite Friday offer, 26% off annual plans with the code LITEFRIDAY26 and a banner saying it ends on 18 December.
Subscribers: adding one subscriber to a new group took under a minute, but the subscriber showed in the list only about 30 seconds after the Saved message.

Campaign: a regular campaign starts from 130 templates or a blank canvas. The test email arrived in the inbox, not in spam, sent from a temporary address because no domain was connected; MailerLite asked us to connect a domain for better delivery.
Automations: the page was empty and offered 18 templates, three of them marked Premium. We did not build one.

Plans: Plan and Billing showed the Free plan (up to 250 subscribers, 2,500 emails, 0 a month) while the header said 14-day trial. The upgrade screen listed Comfort at $12 a month and Power at $25 a month for 500 subscribers.
Checkout: Comfort monthly showed EUR 11 plus 21% VAT, EUR 13.31 due now, with the line 'You will be charged full amount immediately', although 14 trial days were left. We stopped before paying.
Export: a subscriber export to CSV was ready at once.
not_tested: delivery of a real campaign to subscribers, because we sent only a test email to ourselves
